avenues.name: Neutral atoms
avenues.thesis: Rydberg-linked atoms in laser tweezers; the logical-count leader. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch2): can the loss-instrumentation stack (detect → locate → decode → replace) run inside deep logical circuits faster than the loss it manages, on one atomic species, at scale?

avenues.name: Superconducting
avenues.thesis: Aluminium-circuit transmons at ~15 mK; the most industrially mature platform, with below-threshold error correction demonstrated. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch3): can it cut control-and-readout cost per qubit — lines, heat, helium — by ~2 orders of magnitude faster than qubit demand grows, while adding the long-range connectivity its own efficiency codes require?

avenues.name: Trapped ions
avenues.thesis: Identical charged atoms in a shuttling QCCD, all-to-all connected, holding the field's best fidelities and minutes of coherence. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch4): can the refrigeration-and-transport workflow that eats ~95-98% of wall-clock (gates are only ~2%) be engineered down 2-3 orders of magnitude before the fast platforms' fidelity catches up?

avenues.name: Photonics
avenues.thesis: Single photons in silicon-nitride waveguides; room-temperature, natively networked, foundry-fabricated, most-capitalized platform — and the only one with zero below-threshold logical qubits. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch5): a two-layer race — industrial decibel-reduction is winning at the component layer while GKP state quality is losing (still above threshold); can both cross the line before rivals with below-threshold logical qubits compound their lead?

avenues.name: Silicon spin
avenues.thesis: Transistor-sized spin qubits printed on 300mm CMOS lines, coherence to seconds, unit cells above 99% fidelity — but the largest foundry array is eight qubits. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch6): can per-site excellence survive exponentiation (array yield falls off as roughly y to the power N)? The foundry is a proven device factory, not yet an array factory.

avenues.name: Engineered qubits (topological + bosonic/cat)
avenues.thesis: Redesign the qubit so it is intrinsically protected: topological Majorana devices, and cat qubits whose bit flips are suppressed exponentially by construction. Binding constraint restated at bedrock (Ch7): existence and extrapolation. For topological, can the protecting object be shown to exist to the field's satisfaction, when the flagship parity result and a substantive challenge to it now both carry the same journal's peer review? For cat, can the measured single-mode exponent survive gates, ancillas and concatenation at the suppression the roadmaps assume, when the one end-to-end logical measurement improved by about 1.06 across two code distances?

avenues.name: B1 — compute gap closes where storage won
avenues.thesis: By 2027-12-31, a public hardware demonstration (not simulation) of a two-qubit logical gate on a qLDPC code with encoding rate ≥ 1/2.

avenues.name: B2 — platform of that first demonstration
avenues.thesis: Conditional on B1 resolving TRUE: the platform named in the resolving paper is neutral atoms.

avenues.name: B3 — a vendor roadmap, scored not repeated
avenues.thesis: By 2026-12-31, IBM publicly reports Kookaburra operating as a qLDPC memory with a logical processing unit, per its stated 2026 roadmap.

avenues.name: B4 — reloading meets error correction
avenues.thesis: By 2027-12-31, a hardware experiment demonstrates repeated QEC rounds on at least one logical qubit while lost atoms are replaced mid-experiment by continuous or mid-circuit reloading — a logical qubit not lifetime-bounded by the single-atom trap lifetime.

avenues.name: B5 — the umbilical starts to disappear
avenues.thesis: By 2028-06-30, a hardware experiment demonstrates >= 20 superconducting qubits whose control AND readout both reach room temperature via shared or optical I/O (zero dedicated per-qubit coax), sustaining two-qubit gate fidelity >= 99% on the same device.

avenues.name: B6 — the heartbeat accelerates
avenues.thesis: By 2028-06-30, a trapped-ion experiment demonstrates a complete QEC cycle (full syndrome-extraction round on >= 1 error-corrected logical qubit, including all required transport and cooling) with total wall-clock time at most 100 microseconds.

avenues.name: B7 — the pulse crosses the line
avenues.thesis: By 2028-12-31, a photonic platform publicly reports optical GKP states generated on an integrated (on-chip) platform whose measured quality the publishing team itself states to be at or below the relevant fault-tolerance threshold of its stated architecture.

avenues.name: B8 — the array clears its throat
avenues.thesis: By 2028-12-31, a silicon spin platform publicly demonstrates repeated stabilizer-based QEC — at least two full syndrome-extraction rounds with mid-circuit measurement on the same encoded logical qubit — on a device fabricated in an industrial 300mm (or equivalent production-line) process.

avenues.name: B9 — the qubit, not the parity
avenues.thesis: By 2029-06-30, a peer-reviewed journal publication reports a topological (Majorana-based) qubit on which at least two non-commuting logical operations are performed on the same encoded qubit, with a quantitative error rate stated for at least one of them. Preprints do not resolve it.

avenues.name: B10 — the exponent shows up in the logical error
avenues.thesis: By 2028-12-31, a cat-qubit or comparable bosonic-plus-repetition platform publicly reports a logical qubit memory whose measured logical error per cycle improves by a factor of at least 2 between two code distances measured on the same device.

avenues.name: B11 — the referee gap persists
avenues.thesis: By 2027-12-31, no peer-reviewed publication or artifact-committed preprint (by any group, this dossier's lineage included) places at least four of the six audited multiplier claims on a single stated baseline with a single stated accounting. Resolves TRUE if none exists on the date, by documented search.

avenues.name: B12 — the megaquop clock
avenues.thesis: By 2031-12-31, at least one platform publicly demonstrates a megaquop-class computation: at least 1e6 error-corrected logical operations on at least 50 logical qubits, with measured logical error rates reported.

avenues.name: B13 — the platform
avenues.thesis: Conditional on B12 resolving TRUE: the platform of the first megaquop-class demonstration is neutral atoms.

checks._comment: Single source of truth for the consistency-check RULES. Both index.html's console and verification/verify_numbers.py read these, so a threshold can never drift between the page and the verifier. Change a rule HERE and both sides enforce it on next run. (The check LOGIC is still written in each language — see AUTHORING.md — but the rules it enforces live only here.)
